title: Velovate Channel Intro & Integration Framing
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Velovate Cloudworks to evaluate channel reseller and edge-GPU integration patterns. Covered go-to-market motions, basic technical constraints (VPC, on-prem proxies, KMS), pricing signals for reseller margins, and a pilot framing for a 6-week integration and benchmark. Agreed to follow up with security docs and a joint pilot statement of work.
topics: Edge GPU integration patterns and on-prem gateway
Pilot scope: benchmarks, SLA targets, and success criteria
action_items: Evan Park: Share partner-integration-patterns.docx and reseller pricing sheet (due 2026-07-07)
Sofia Gutierrez: Draft initial pilot runbook and GPU benchmark template (due 2026-07-09)
Marcus Holt (Velovate): Provide SOC2 report and KMS/HSM vendor details (due 2026-07-08)
Jonas Petrov (Velovate): Confirm expected traffic profile and typical sequence lengths for edge workloads (due 2026-07-06)
next_steps: Redwood to send security packet and SOC2 link
Schedule technical deep dive with Velovate infra team (proposed: 2026-07-09)
Velovate to nominate internal pilot owners and legal contact for reseller MSA
Agree pilot KPIs and schedule 6-week pilot kickoff
transcript: [00:00] Evan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood inference, account lead. Sofia and Priya from our side are here too. How's everyone doing?

[00:14] Anika Rao: Hi Evan, good, thanks. We are excited to chat — I'm Anika from Velovate Partnerships, with Jonas and Marcus from platform and security. Quick apology, Lina's on but might have to drop early.

[00:28] Sofia Gutierrez: Great, thanks. The goal here is just to understand Velovate's channel motion and technical constraints so we can sketch an integration pattern. We'll ask some questions and then propose a pilot model.

[00:42] Jonas Petrov: Sounds good. High level: Velovate resells edge GPU capacity to telco and retail customers. We run a small fleet of on-prem boxes and hybrid clouds. Our customers want a managed LLM inference endpoint that can be routed to cloud or local edge depending on latency. We're exploring Redwood for both hosted and private options behind our gateway.
[00:58] Evan Park: Nice. When you say gateway, is that a Velovate-managed edge proxy or something you'd expect Redwood to bundle?

[01:06] Jonas Petrov: It's Velovate-managed. We have an edge gateway that terminates customer traffic and then shunts inference to either local GPU or public cloud backends. Ideally Redwood would run as a private deployment in our VPC or as a lightweight runtime in our edge clusters, and the gateway would route by policy.

[01:24] Sofia Gutierrez: Okay, two integration paths we typically see: 1) private deployment inside a customer/VPC with our control plane managed by Redwood but data stays in-cust, and 2) lightweight on-prem runtime (air-gapped option) with a small control plane connection. Both support autoscaling and can be pinned to model versions. Which resonates?

[01:42] Anika Rao: Both, but for reseller customers the path that requires minimal ops is attractive. We want something we can bundle as a service — so a managed private deployment with an option for a small runtime at the very edge for ultra-low latency seems ideal.

[01:58] Marcus Holt: Security is our big gating item. We need SSO, SAML integration with our customer portal, audit logs ingestion into our SIEM, and KMS/HSM for key management. Also data residency — some customers in EU require logs and model inputs to remain in-region.

[02:12] Priya Nair: Understood. We support SAML/SSO and can push audit logs to your syslog/ingest endpoints; our private deployments can be configured to use customer-managed KMS. For region constraints, Redwood routing can pin to region-specific instances and fallback to an approved model variant if capacity isn't available.

[02:30] Jonas Petrov: On the runtime side, a couple of practical questions: what's the smallest GPU footprint you support? We use a mix of A10G and older T4s at the edge. Also curious about quantized model support and KV cache behavior for chat workloads.

[02:44] Sofia Gutierrez: We have runtime profiles for different families. T4/A10G are supported; for older gen we recommend lower sequence length and batch sizing to maintain latency SLOs. For quantization, we have variants that trade quality for token cost — those are often good for high-throughput but less critical QA flows. KV cache is preserved across warm sessions and we can expose TTL config so your gateway can control session affinity.
[03:10] Anika Rao: From the partnership side, we need a reseller pricing sheet and how margins could work. Do you do co-sell credits or a marketplace listing?

[03:20] Evan Park: We do both. For early partners we typically offer a rev-share model or a discounted committed capacity option (Redwood Dedicated) that Velovate could resell. We also support a marketplace listing with co-marketing credits after a pilot. We'll include a partner pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[03:36] Marcus Holt: Any compliance background you can share upfront? SOC2 type II? ISO? Our procurement team will want to see reports.

[03:44] Priya Nair: Yes, SOC2 Type II, and we have an ISO overview; we also provide a security pack with architecture diagrams and recommended network ACLs for VPC/private deployments. We'll send the packet after this call.

[03:58] Jonas Petrov: Good. For the pilot, we're thinking of a representative retail use-case: short chat completions with ~60 token replies, heavy read traffic but occasional long tail. We'll want to measure p95 latency and token cost per 1k requests. Does Redwood have a benchmark harness we can run?

[04:14] Sofia Gutierrez: We have a benchmark template; Sofia will share a GPU benchmark spreadsheet and a runbook so you can run both synthetic and real prompt sets. For the edge, we'd recommend running the pilot on a small A10G cluster to validate latency. We'll include guidance on batch sizing and KV cache settings.
[04:34] Anika Rao: On timelines, how fast could we get a pilot moving? Assuming legal and security checks don't block, can we do a pilot in 4–6 weeks?

[04:42] Evan Park: Yes, 6 weeks is realistic. Week 0 for provisioning and SSO/KMS config, week 1–2 for basic integration and bench setup, week 3–5 for load and quality checks, final week for analysis and go/no-go. We'll propose a kickoff calendar after we share the SOW draft.
[04:58] Jonas Petrov: One more technical nit: does Redwood support on-prem GPU orchestration that lets us keep the KV cache on local disk? Some of our devices are intermittently connected.

[05:08] Priya Nair: Intermittent connectivity is a known pattern. We support local KV persistence with configurable eviction and sync-to-cloud strategies. For offline-first flows we recommend local runtime + periodic reconcile to a cloud cache, but we can discuss durability tradeoffs for your fleet.
[05:26] Lina Gomes: Quick question about billing — is metered per token only or do you also bill for reserved capacity?

[05:33] Evan Park: Both. Hosted usage is metered per token and embeddings units; Dedicated/reserved is a capacity contract (monthly commit) and we can set up billed overage rules. For reseller deals, committed capacity often gives the cleanest margin.
[05:48] Anika Rao: Regarding co-marketing, we typically want a joint press brief and a reference architecture diagram in the marketplace listing. Are those items you support?

[05:56] Priya Nair: Yes, after a successful pilot we can provide a joint case study, reference diagram, and assist on marketplace listing copy and artwork. We also have a partner portal with assets for co-marketing.
[06:10] Marcus Holt: Data retention — can you set retention to zero for certain classes of traffic or drop logs after N days? Some of our customers require minimal telemetry retention.

[06:18] Sofia Gutierrez: We have retention controls per route; for private deployments we can set retention to minimal or route logs to your SIEM only. We'll capture these options in the security packet.
[06:32] Jonas Petrov: Any known limitations around model types for edge? For example running quantized Llama variants or transformer architectures with longcontext?

[06:42] Priya Nair: We support a curated catalog of open models optimized for inference. Long-context models are supported but require memory considerations; for edge we recommend model splits or lower context lengths. We'll share recommended model profiles for A10G and T4.
[06:58] Anika Rao: Who would be our go-to for day-to-day? Is it an AE or partner manager?

[07:04] Evan Park: I'll be your AE initially; we also have a partner manager and solution engineer (Sofia) who will coordinate technical work. If the program scales we'll assign a dedicated partner manager and on-call SE.
[07:18] Jonas Petrov: Ok, sounds good. On the subject of fallback behavior: if an edge host fails do you provide an automatic fallback to a cloud-hosted variant?

[07:26] Sofia Gutierrez: Yes, our smart routing supports policy-based fallback to region or cloud. You can define cost vs latency preferences and failover models; one caveat is that model variants should be compatible for deterministic fallbacks (e.g., same tokenization and similar output distribution).
[07:44] Anika Rao: For the pilot SOW, can we include joint success metrics — e.g., p95 < 180ms for edge requests, cost per 1k tokens under X, and error rate < 0.5%?
[07:53] Evan Park: Yep, those are reasonable to aim for. We'll propose target KPIs in the SOW and leave room for measurement noise and tuning.
[08:04] Marcus Holt: A procurement note — we typically require a reseller addendum and simple indemnity. Who handles legal on your side?
[08:11] Priya Nair: Our legal team can work with yours. We'll include a reseller MSA template; legal will follow once we have the contact email.
[08:20] Jonas Petrov: I'm going to flag an internal question around resource tagging and billing — can we get per-customer token telemetry and per-route cost breakdowns?
[08:29] Sofia Gutierrez: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns by API key/route and we can push usage hooks to billing systems. That should satisfy per-customer chargeback needs.
[08:40] Anika Rao: Perfect. Anything else from your side?
[08:44] Evan Park: One ask: please share a short list of 2–3 pilot customers (non-sensitive) so we can map architecture and expected traffic. That will help Sofia design the bench drives.
[08:55] Anika Rao: We'll do that. We'll also gather SOC2 and KMS details and get them over. Lina may drop at 30 minutes but she'll send follow-ups.
[09:04] Lina Gomes: Quick note — for co-marketing we also prefer a joint webinar rather than just a press brief. Happy to discuss later.
[09:12] Evan Park: Great. We'll note webinar as an option. Okay, if there are no more open items let's recap next steps.
[09:20] Jonas Petrov: Quick clarifying question on KV cache TTL: Can we set different TTLs per customer route?
[09:26] Priya Nair: Yes, per-route TTLs and session affinity config are supported. We'll include config examples in the runbook.

[09:36] Evan Park: Recap: Redwood will share security packet, partner pricing, integration patterns doc, and benchmark spreadsheet. Velovate will share SOC2 link, KMS vendor info, traffic profile, and pilot customer list. We'll propose a technical deep dive for 2026-07-09. Anything to add?
[09:54] Anika Rao: That covers it. Thanks everyone, we'll look for the materials and coordinate internal stakeholders.
[10:02] Evan Park: Thanks all — we'll follow up with an email and attach the items. Talk soon.
